item.description:
作者：Aaron Levie 账号：@levie 简介：ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
Any form of security through obscurity is fully over. This barely worked as a method with humans, but just simply is over in a world of autonomous systems that will look through every crevice and try every permutation of attack possible.
As a result, years and years of legacy enterprise infrastructure will need to be upgraded, security practices modernized, data pipelines cleaned up, access controls better managed, and much more. Agents will help on the defensive side because they can both accelerate this work and equally simulate the risk vectors.
But there’s a long road ahead to prepare for this future. This is also partially why diffusion timelines will take longer than some realize.

item.description:
作者：Madhu Guru 账号：@realmadhuguru 简介：Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
If you feel stuck in your career, stop waiting for clarity. create it through action.
A lot of PMs reaching out for advice tell me they feel stuck as AI rapidly changes their role.
They want to get into AI but don’t know where to start and are afraid.
This inertia kills clarity…the solution to this is action.
Build something, automate a workflow, connect with people who inspire you.
Each action gives you experience, feedback and new ideas.
Clarity is often the consequence of action.
Send this to a friend who needs to hear it.

item.title: David Silver and Lasse Espeholt of Ineffable Intelligence: A Superlearner for the Age of Experience
item.description:
播客：Training Data
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:32 Collectively, you know, we started with this kind of gray mush in our head. We somehow started out knowing nothing at all and somehow discovered, like, everything that humans know today was, like, this process of collective discovery, like, of of languages and technology and science and mathematics and all the rest of it. Know, everything we learned, we discovered it for ourselves. And that's an incredible thing that no one has cracked yet in AI. And so to me, that is the essence of what it will take to get to superintelligence, like a system that can just keep learning and discovering knowledge forever.
Speaker 2 | 00:49 - 01:10 I'm thrilled to have Dave Silver and Lesae Espeholt with us, two of the co founders of ineffable intelligence. Great name, by the way. Fun fact, Dave, you were the first person I cold emailed to come on training data when we started the show 100 ish episodes ago. And it feels like a full circle moment to finally have you on the show. So thank you for joining us.
Speaker 1 | 01:11 - 01:11 Thank you.
Speaker 2 | 01:12 - 01:43 Dave, let's start with you. Your 2009 PhD was on reinforcement learning applied to the devilishly difficult game of Go. You demonstrated for the world for the first time that superhuman in one domain machine intelligence was possible. And I think you were really the figure that inspired the entire current generation of reinforcement learning and deep learning researchers. And so thank you for your contributions to where the field is.
Speaker 2 | 01:44 - 01:57 I'm curious, thinking back to that point in time, what did you learn? What did you have conviction on? And what has remained the same and what has changed as AI has changed over the last five years or so?
Speaker 1 | 01:57 - 02:47 Yeah. Thank you, and pleasure to be here, and I'm glad I finally made it after these 100 episodes. It's a pleasure to be here. So I suppose I always had this conviction starting my PhD and going into the game of Go that the right approach to solve AI was through learning from experience, through systems that discovered things for themselves, that were learning through reinforcement learning to get better and better and better, and that that would be the thing which would lead to the emergence of intelligence and ultimately superintelligence. And so I suppose we were able to show that in the game of Go, but it's a conviction that has held true throughout my career, and here we are now applying that conviction, ineffable, trying to show that indeed superintelligence can emerge all the way through systems that learn from experience.
Speaker 1 | 02:48 - 03:39 And in terms of things which are different, although we are not pursuing the human data path that the LLM world has pursued, I do think there's lots of interesting lessons to learn from that. In particular, it was definitely a surprise to me how a system that was trained on a massive amount of data could then be very quickly fine tuned on a very small amount of data to completely change its behavior. That was something which I think was something which changed my mindset in terms of just suggesting that if you get things at the right scale, that a lot of things which seem incredibly hard or they might be very slow, that once you've kind of experienced enough data, that after that, the things that were slow can become very fast. I think that's a lesson that wasn't obvious to me in advance until it happened.
Speaker 2 | 03:39 - 03:56 Okay, we're going to come back to that later. You could have run this program inside DeepMind where could have probably had more access to compute than just about anybody. You decided the right thing to do was to start a new lab. Why'd you do that?
Speaker 1 | 03:57 - 04:31 Yeah. So look, first of all, I had a fantastic time at DeepMind. I loved my years there, and I have a huge amount of respect for the people there and still got on with them very well. But at the end of the day, I have a really strong belief about how we can go beyond where we are today with AI and all the way to superintelligence, And the path that I believe in doesn't actually go through LLM based products as an intermediate point. And when I really thought about that, I thought about it really hard.
Speaker 1 | 04:31 - 05:44 I realized that I felt that so passionately that this deserved to be more than just the corner of an organization that's focused on LLM based products and deserved to be represented by an elite AI lab that really just gives this approach its all and represents it 100%. Once I realized that, it felt very natural to create this company. I suppose another way to look at it is that the world already has tens of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands, of really talented researchers all pursuing exactly the same approach, really just doubling down on LLMs with pre training, post training, coding, and that kind of LLM path, am I going to be the 100,001 person that's pursuing that approach? Is that the most effective use of my time and my energy? And in the end, I realized that there's this other lamppost that right now no one is looking under and where if I actually put my effort there, has a much higher chance of really having a massive impact on the field because if this works, it's going to change the whole of AI.
Speaker 1 | 05:45 - 05:54 So I think that kind of realization also meant that this was something which just means that it's the best way to have impact upon the field through this approach.
Speaker 2 | 05:55 - 05:58 Plus, you had a company name that couldn't go to waste, so...
Speaker 1 | 05:58 - 05:58 That's right. Yeah, it's right.
Speaker 2 | 05:58 - 06:00 Do want to say where the mind's called Ineffable?
Speaker 1 | 06:00 - 06:54 Yeah.
